concerns.text: FR-002 says 'normalize features per cell' but does not restrict normalization statistics to the first-50-cycle window. If per-cell normalization uses statistics computed over the FULL trace (including late-life cycles), future information leaks into the early-cycle predictors, inflating R². Specify that normalization statistics are computed from the first 50 cycles only (or from training-set aggregates).

SC-003 validates 'interpretability validity' by consistency between permutation importance and SHAP. Both methods probe the SAME trained model; their agreement measures method convergence, not whether the identified signatures are scientifically valid predictors of degradation. This is a weak, near-circular validation target. Add an independent check, e.g. that top-ranked features alone (e.g. linear regression on the identified time-steps/channels) retain predictive power, or comparison against known electrochemical degradation markers.

R² ≥ 0.80 is required on a held-out set of cells with entirely unseen cycling protocols, but NASA Ames (~tens of cells) and UW datasets yield very small per-protocol cell counts. R² on a handful of held-out cells is statistically unstable and the 0.80 threshold may be unattainable for reasons of sample size rather than model quality. The spec should state a minimum held-out subset size or report uncertainty on R², and treat 0.80 as a target rather than a pass/fail gate for the unseen-protocol subset.

The target is variously called 'final capacity fade', 'remaining useful life' (US-2 Scenario 2), and 'predicted_fade'. Capacity fade (a scalar health metric) and RUL (cycles to EOL threshold) are different quantities in battery science. Define the target precisely — e.g. fade = (Q_initial − Q_final)/Q_initial at a fixed cycle count or EOL criterion — and use one term consistently.
